templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Despite the fact that the economy is growing, the gap between the rich and the poor continues to widen. The government must intervene with targeted welfare schemes.'
Assumption I: Economic growth alone does not reduce inequality.
Assumption II: Government welfare schemes can reduce the rich-poor gap.
Assumption III: The government has not yet introduced welfare schemes.
Assumption IV: Economic growth benefits only the wealthy.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: I is directly implied — growth isn't enough (implicit). II is the logic behind 'must intervene' — implicit. III is not assumed — existing schemes may be insufficient. IV is an extreme claim not assumed. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'In order to reduce the burden on courts, the government should promote Lok Adalats and alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.'
Assumption I: Courts are overburdened with pending cases.
Assumption II: Lok Adalats can effectively resolve disputes.
Assumption III: People are willing to use alternative dispute mechanisms.
Assumption IV: Alternative mechanisms are cheaper than courts.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Court overburdening (I) is the stated motivation — implicit. Lok Adalats being effective (II) is assumed for the suggestion to make sense. People's willingness (III) is necessary for the mechanism to work — implicit. Cost advantage (IV) is not assumed. I, II and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'It is essential that India diversifies its export basket beyond IT and software services to sustain long-term economic growth.'
Assumption I: India's current exports are dominated by IT and software.
Assumption II: Relying on limited sectors poses risks to economic stability.
Assumption III: Diversification will automatically lead to growth.
Assumption IV: India has the capacity to develop other export sectors.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: I (IT dominance) is the premise of the argument — implicit. II (risk of limited sectors) is the logic behind 'essential' — implicit. III is too deterministic — 'diversification will automatically' is not assumed. IV (capacity to diversify) is assumed since the suggestion is made — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The Central government should provide incentives to states that achieve high levels of female literacy.'
Assumption I: Female literacy rates vary across states.
Assumption II: Incentives motivate state governments to improve literacy.
Assumption III: Female literacy is an important development indicator.
Assumption IV: States with low female literacy lack resources.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Variation across states (I) justifies a performance-based scheme — implicit. Incentives motivating action (II) is the mechanism assumed — implicit. Female literacy being important (III) is why it's incentivised — implicit. IV (resource constraint) is not assumed — low literacy may have other causes. I, II and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Corruption at grassroots level erodes public trust more than high-level scams because it affects daily life directly.'
Assumption I: Corruption exists at both grassroots and high levels.
Assumption II: Public trust is damaged more when daily life is affected.
Assumption III: High-level scams do not affect public trust at all.
Assumption IV: Reducing grassroots corruption should be a priority.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: I (corruption at both levels) is the comparison being made — implicit. II (daily life impact = greater trust erosion) is the reasoning — implicit. III is the opposite of what's implied — high-level scams do affect trust, just less. IV is an implied recommendation — not directly stated as an assumption. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'A newspaper editorial: The government's decision to privatise public sector banks may expose depositors to greater financial risks.'
Assumption I: Private banks are riskier than public sector banks.
Assumption II: The government has announced privatisation of public sector banks.
Assumption III: Depositor safety is a concern of the editorial.
Assumption IV: Public sector banks are currently protecting depositors.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: I (private banks riskier) is the implied assumption behind 'greater risks' — implicit. II (decision announced) is the trigger for the editorial — implicit. III is the purpose of the editorial — implicit. IV (public banks protecting depositors) is assumed as a comparison baseline — implicit. All four are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'India needs to invest heavily in research and development to remain competitive in the global technology race.'
Assumption I: India's current R&D investment is insufficient.
Assumption II: R&D investment leads to technological competitiveness.
Assumption III: India is currently losing the global technology race.
Assumption IV: India has the scientific talent to benefit from R&D investment.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Insufficient current R&D (I) is why 'heavy investment' is called for — implicit. R&D leading to competitiveness (II) is the assumed mechanism — implicit. III (currently losing) is too strong — the statement says 'to remain competitive' implying current standing is at risk. IV (talent) is assumed since investment is recommended — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'A noted economist argued that artificial intelligence will create more jobs than it destroys, provided governments invest in reskilling the workforce.'
Assumption I: AI will destroy some existing jobs.
Assumption II: New jobs created by AI require different skills.
Assumption III: Governments are currently not investing in reskilling.
Assumption IV: Workers can acquire new skills through reskilling programmes.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: AI destroying some jobs (I) is the premise — implicit. New skills being required (II) explains the need for reskilling — implicit. III (no current investment) — the statement says 'provided they invest' which doesn't imply they're not currently. IV (workers can reskill) is assumed for reskilling to be viable — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'India's diplomatic relations with its neighbours are the key to ensuring regional peace and stability.'
Assumption I: India shares diplomatic relations with its neighbours.
Assumption II: Regional peace depends on India's diplomatic actions.
Assumption III: India's current relations with its neighbours are stable.
Assumption IV: Good diplomatic relations prevent conflicts.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Diplomatic relations existing (I) is the basis of the statement — implicit. Regional peace depending on India's relations (II) is the core claim — implicit. III (currently stable) is not assumed — the statement may be aspirational. Good relations preventing conflict (IV) is the mechanism — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The judiciary must remain independent of the executive to uphold the rule of law and protect citizens' rights.'
Assumption I: An independent judiciary is essential for rule of law.
Assumption II: There are attempts to influence the judiciary by the executive.
Assumption III: Citizens' rights are currently being violated.
Assumption IV: An executive-controlled judiciary would undermine citizens' rights.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Independent judiciary = rule of law (I) is the core assumption — implicit. Executive influence attempts (II) explains the 'must remain' urgency — implicit. III (rights being violated) is not directly assumed. IV (executive control undermining rights) is the risk being guarded against — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'India's per capita carbon emissions are far below the global average, so developed nations have a greater responsibility to lead climate action.'
Assumption I: Per capita emissions are a fair measure of climate responsibility.
Assumption II: Developed nations have higher per capita emissions than India.
Assumption III: Historical emissions should determine climate responsibility.
Assumption IV: India should not be required to reduce its emissions.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Per capita being a fair measure (I) is why it's cited — implicit. Developed nations having higher per capita (II) is the factual basis — implicit. III (historical emissions) is a separate argument not made here. IV (India not needing to reduce) — statement says developed nations should lead, not that India is exempt. I and II are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The policy of reservations has been in place for over seven decades; it is time to assess whether the intended beneficiaries have actually benefited and whether the policy needs revision.'
Assumption I: Reservations were intended to benefit certain groups.
Assumption II: Seven decades is sufficient time to evaluate a policy's impact.
Assumption III: The reservation policy may not have fully benefited the intended groups.
Assumption IV: Reservations are no longer needed.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Reservation having intended beneficiaries (I) is the baseline — implicit. Seven decades being enough to evaluate (II) justifies 'it is time' — implicit. Possible incomplete benefit (III) is why a review is needed — implicit. IV (no longer needed) is not assumed — revision could mean strengthening, not eliminating. I, II and III are implicit.

incorrect: Ask: is it taken for granted? 🤔
